Introduction and meaning
Sexual harassment (old 354A): unwelcome physical contact and advances; a demand or request for sexual favours; showing pornography against her will; sexually coloured remarks. Remarks are the lighter band.
In student language: BNS s. 75 is the rule on “Sexual harassment”. The section provides that (1) A man committing any of the following acts:—. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 75 exists so that “Sexual harassment” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.

The provision in detail
75. (1) A man committing any of the following acts:—

(i) physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures; or

(ii) a demand or request for sexual favours; or

(iii) showing pornography against the will of a woman; or

(iv) making sexually coloured remarks,

shall be guilty of the offence of sexual harassment

(2) Any man who commits the offence specified in clause (i) or clause (ii) or clause (iii) of sub-section (1) shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both

(3) Any man who commits the offence specified in clause (iv) of sub-section (1) shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both

Essential ingredients
1. (1) A man committing any of the following acts:—
2. (i) physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures; or
3. (ii) a demand or request for sexual favours; or

6. shall be guilty of the offence of sexual harassment
7. (2) Any man who commits the offence specified in clause
8. (1) shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
9. (3) Any man who commits the offence specified in clause
10. (1) shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both

examples.title: Example 1 — simple (teaching example)
examples.body: A short everyday fact pattern is tested against “Sexual harassment”. Name BNS s. 75, list the ingredients, and say which facts match. This is a teaching example — the statute does not print a numbered illustration under this heading.

examples.title: Example 2 — practical application / distinction (teaching example)
examples.body: Change one ingredient so that BNS s. 75 fails. A complex problem or motion often hinges on this subtle missing ingredient. State the failure expressly. Label this as an example, never as a reported case.

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 75 (Sexual harassment) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 75 (Sexual harassment), Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) (1) A man committing any of the following acts:—
   (2) (i) physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures; or
   (3) (ii) a demand or request for sexual favours; or
   (4) (iii) showing pornography against the will of a woman; or
   (5) (iv) making sexually coloured remarks,
   (6) shall be guilty of the offence of sexual harassment
   (7) (2) Any man who commits the offence specified in clause
   (8) (1) shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 75 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 75 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

rows.right: Read the neighbour’s title on its own page before you write.

rows.left: (1) A man committing any of the following acts:—
rows.right: Different ingredients — do not paste this section’s test onto the neighbour.

rows.left: Citing a neighbour as if it were s. 75.
rows.right: Citing s. 75 where the neighbour actually applies.

misconceptions.trap: Writing only the section number and title without analyzing ingredients or case ratio.
misconceptions.correction: An authoritative note defines the concept, lists ingredients, uses an illustration, states explanations/exceptions, applies the test, and concludes with BNS s. 75.

misconceptions.trap: Copying a statutory illustration without mapping it to an ingredient.
misconceptions.correction: Quote the illustration, then write which ingredient it proves or which ingredient is missing. Mapping is the core evidentiary link.

misconceptions.trap: Giving a one-line summary or shortened explanation of the provision.
misconceptions.correction: Authoritative chamber practice and judicial papers require a complete answer. The analysis on this page is written at full length for that reason.

Introduction. BNS s. 75 deals with Sexual harassment. It sits in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. After 1 July 2024 this is the current-law citation for this offence / definition / punishment.

Meaning. Sexual harassment (old 354A): unwelcome physical contact and advances; a demand or request for sexual favours; showing pornography against her will; sexually coloured remarks. Remarks are the lighter band.

An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Essential ingredients. An authoritative analysis must list them, not hide them in one paragraph:

2. (i) physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures; or
3. (ii) a demand or request for sexual favours; or

6. shall be guilty of the offence of sexual harassment

Illustration. Give one short original example (label it as an example) and apply the ingredients.

Limitations. Apply only the conditions written in s. 75. Do not import a defence from a different chapter unless the question requires it.

Comprehensive Written Submissions. Deepen the doctrinal synthesis with four foundational layers.

Layer 1 — Place the section in the Chapter. Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.. Show why this heading sits where it sits.

Layer 2 — Work a second, slightly harder hypothetical. Change one ingredient and show why the section then fails.

Layer 3 — Distinction. Contrast BNS s. 75 with BNS s. 74, BNS s. 79. Write a short table in prose: meaning, ingredients, stage of the case, consequence. Confusion of neighbouring sections is the most common reason arguments collapse under judicial scrutiny.



Layer 5 — Application and current-law close. Apply the test to the problem facts in IRAC form (Issue, Rule, Application, Conclusion). Close with: “The governing citation on or after 1 July 2024 is BNS s. 75.”

Ingredients first, illustration second, application third, conclusion last.

revisionPoints: First ingredient: (1) A man committing any of the following acts:—
No printed illustration — prepare an original labelled example.

For offences on or after 1 July 2024, the correct citation is BNS s. 75 — Sexual harassment. Older books and judgments may still print a historical number (354A). Convert it. Write the BNS number in a current answer. Do not treat the old number as if it were still the law.
